body:
this should indeed be handled inside `getClientIps` if `unknown` is a common bad value.

but anyway, I also suggest you to report the bug to Squid. Otherwise all your requests will be reported as coming from the Squid server IP.

Apparently, this is something that can be configured in Squid: http://www.squid-cache.org/Doc/config/forwarded_for/

```
If set to "on", Squid will append your client's IP address
in the HTTP requests it forwards. By default it looks like:

    X-Forwarded-For: 192.1.2.3

If set to "off", it will appear as

    X-Forwarded-For: unknown
```

When Squid is used as a trusted reverse proxy, it must be configured with `forwarded_for on`. But apparently that's not the situation met by @skonsoft.

Here, Squid is an enterprise proxy (not trusted).

```
      CLIENT          |         SERVER
Browser   >  Squid    > Trusted Proxy > Symfony
192.0.0.1   193.1.2.3      10.1.2.3
```

With trusted proxy, you get headers like this:

```
Remote-Addr: 10.1.2.3               # The trusted proxy
X-Forwarded-For: unknown,193.1.2.3  # unknown from Squid + Squid output IP added by the trusted proxy
```

You cannot return blindly return the `REMOTE_ADDR` when `X-Forwarded-For` contains an invalid IP address. Instead, an invalid IP address must be removed in [`Request::getClientIps()`](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/v2.8.0-BETA1/src/Symfony/Component/HttpFoundation/Request.php#L825-L834).

`unknown` is a standardized value, but other "obfuscated" values can be set.
https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239#section-6.2

What do you think about check ip address by `filtervar(..., FILTER_VALIDATE_IP)` here:
https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/9610602ab5df64118d8b2fabeca4a70d1eda4e11/src/Symfony/Component/HttpFoundation/Request.php#L830 and if it invalid - exclude it?

I was trying to implement this, but removing invalid IP addresses is incompatible with an existing test : 
[`RequestTest::testGetClientIpsForwarded() #1`](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/9610602ab5df64118d8b2fabeca4a70d1eda4e11/src/Symfony/Component/HttpFoundation/Tests/RequestTest.php#L861)

It asserts that if the `Forwarded` header contains `for="_gazonk"`, then this value is returned as client IP. We can ask @tony-co what were the motivations of [this test case](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/pull/11379/files#diff-ff258be5f9da1f743abc56d08e1affd3R895).

@GromNaN, I think `_gazonk` test case is wrong.

@stof, what do you think?

issue.title: [Request] Ignore invalid IP addresses sent by proxies

The [RFC 7239](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7239#section-6.2) allows other values that IP addresses to be passed in `Forwarded`header and [Nginx can add `unknown` to the `X-Forwarded-For`header](http://www.squid-cache.org/Doc/config/forwarded_for/).

To prevent these invalid IP addresses from being returned as "Client IP", this PR ensure that they are excluded.
